name: 01_rows_reconcile_end_to_end
check: For every month, raw rows = warehouse rows + excluded rows.
why: Proves the pipeline neither lost nor duplicated a single row between the downloaded files and the warehouse.

name: 02_amounts_reconcile_end_to_end
check: For every month, raw total_amount = warehouse total_amount + excluded total_amount, to the cent.
why: Proves no money was lost or invented. Amounts are summed as DECIMAL so the comparison is exact, with no floating-point rounding drift.

name: 03_views_reconcile_with_fact
check: Every analysis view adds back up to the fact table (row counts and, where stored exactly, amounts).
why: A view with a wrong JOIN can silently drop or duplicate trips; this catches it before a dashboard does.

name: 04_trip_id_unique
why: trip_id is the fact table's key; a duplicate means a trip is counted twice in every metric.

name: 05_required_fields_not_null
check: Columns every metric depends on are never NULL.
why: NULL keys drop trips from joins; NULL amounts or times silently shrink sums and averages.

name: 06_foreign_keys
check: Every foreign key in fact_trips exists in its dimension (no orphan keys).
why: An orphan key makes a trip vanish from any chart that uses that dimension, so totals disagree between pages.

name: 07_cleaning_rules_hold
check: No trip in the warehouse breaks any Phase 2 exclusion rule.
why: Re-tests the cleaning output independently, so a bug in the cleaning code cannot let impossible trips through unnoticed.

name: 08_dim_date_complete
check: dim_date has every calendar day between its first and last date, with no gaps or duplicates.
why: A missing date makes daily trend lines skip days and makes "per day" averages divide by the wrong number.

name: 09_every_day_has_trips
check: Every date in the study period has at least one trip.
why: A day with zero trips in a city taxi dataset almost certainly means a missing or truncated source file, not a real absence of demand.

name: 10_daily_volume_anomalies
check: No day falls below 0.6 x the median of the same weekday in the same month.
why: A sudden collapse in volume is more often a data problem (partial file, vendor outage) than real demand; holidays and storms are legitimate exceptions to review.

name: 11_tip_recording_gaps
check: No large tip-eligible vendor x rate-code segment records tips on fewer than 5.0% of trips.
why: Phase 4 found rate code 99 records no tips at all. This check catches the NEXT gap like it automatically, instead of relying on someone spotting an odd chart.

name: 12_flag_rate_shifts
check: No quality flag's share of trips moves more than 5.0 percentage points from one month to the next.
why: A sudden shift (like Flex Fare in March 2024) changes how reliable some metrics are; it may be real, but it must be explained before month-to-month comparisons are trusted.

name: 13_monthly_removal_rate
check: Cleaning removes no more than 5.0% of any month's raw rows.
why: Removal rates have been about 2-3%; a jump means either a much dirtier source file or a cleaning rule misbehaving.

name: 14_catchall_zone_share
check: No more than 3.0% of a month's trips start or end in catch-all zones 264/265.
why: Catch-all zones are excluded from maps and zone rankings, so if their share grows, geographic results quietly cover less of the data.
